paper_title: Breaking the Softmax Bottleneck: A High-Rank RNN Language Model

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for its proposed model?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports a word-level test perplexity of 47.69 on Penn Treebank for its proposed model (AWD-LSTM-MoS with dynamic evaluation).

sub_questions.q: In which setting (single model; with dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble or fine-tuning if reported) is the reported Penn Treebank test perplexity achieved?
sub_questions.answer: The reported Penn Treebank test perplexity of 47.69 is achieved in a single model setting with dynamic evaluation (indicated by †).

sub_questions.q: What Penn Treebank test perplexities does the paper list for baseline models?
sub_questions.answer: The paper lists baseline Penn Treebank test perplexities including: 92.0 (RNN-LDA + KN-5 + cache), 82.7 (LSTM), 78.6 (Variational LSTM (MC)), 78.9 (CharCNN), 70.9 (Pointer Sentinel-LSTM), 72.1 (LSTM + continuous cache pointer), 73.2 (Tied Variational LSTM + augmented loss), 65.4 (Variational RHN), 64.0 (NAS Cell), 58.3 (2-layer skip connection LSTM), 58.8 (AWD-LSTM w/o finetune), 57.3 (AWD-LSTM), 52.8 (AWD-LSTM + continuous cache pointer), and 51.1 (AWD-LSTM + dynamic evaluation).
sub_questions.quote: Mikolov & Zweig 2012 – RNN-LDA + KN-5 + cache 9M ‡ - 92.0 ... Krause et al. 2017 – AWD-LSTM + dynamic evaluation † 24M 51.6 51.1

sub_questions.q: How does the proposed model's Penn Treebank test perplexity compare with the baseline models listed in the paper?
sub_questions.answer: The proposed model's Penn Treebank test perplexity of 47.69 outperforms all listed baselines, including the best baseline (AWD-LSTM + dynamic evaluation) which has a test perplexity of 51.1, improving by 3.41 points.
sub_questions.quote: With a comparable number of parameters, MoS outperforms all baselines with or without dynamic evaluation, and substantially improves over the current state of the art, by up to 3.6 points in perplexity.

sub_questions.q: Does the paper report any Penn Treebank test perplexity for the proposed model without dynamic evaluation, and if so, what is it?
sub_questions.answer: Yes, the paper reports a Penn Treebank test perplexity of 55.97 for the proposed model without dynamic evaluation (AWD-LSTM-MoS w/o finetune).
